years_since_diagnosis.evidence: just diagnosed with Crohn's six months ago

severity.evidence: collapsed at a job site from dehydration and severe abdominal pain... fatigue affects my work... joint pain is getting worse... can barely manage 6 [hours of work]... can barely get out of bed... inflammation needs to be controlled to prevent complications, mentioned something about increased colon cancer risk

disease_control.evidence: prednisone immediately, which helped, but he said it's not a long-term solution. Tried mesalamine next, minimal improvement. Then sulfasalazine, which gave me terrible headaches. I've been trying to manage with diet changes and budesonide, but I know it's not enough. The fatigue affects my work... The joint pain is getting worse too, some days I can barely get out of bed.

encounters.evidence: Emergency room visit led to CT scan showing significant inflammation.
They referred me to a GI specialist, took two months to get in. Dr. Williams did a colonoscopy and confirmed Crohn's disease... Now he wants me on a biologic, recommended Entyvio.

status.evidence: Now he wants me on a biologic, recommended Entyvio.

barriers.evidence: The problem is I'm self-employed, my insurance is catastrophic coverage only. The medication would cost me $5,000 per infusion, every 8 weeks. That's impossible.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: Patient went to ER, then referred to GI specialist. No mention of GP/PCP in the referral chain.
